stocks.name: Apple
stocks.summary: Apple’s price slipped 0.8% on the day, keeping it just 0.8% below its 52‑week high and still 37.9% above its low, indicating limited upside near the top of its range. The stock has rallied 8.6% over the month and 24.7% YTD, showing strength despite the near‑high pullback. Watch for upcoming earnings guidance and any macro‑tech demand shifts as the next catalyst.

stocks.name: Microsoft
stocks.summary: Microsoft rose 0.5% intraday, trading 6.9% off its 52‑week peak while remaining 42.1% above its low, comfortably in the upper‑mid range. Gains of 2.7% month‑to‑date and 6.5% YTD reflect steady momentum. Investors should focus on the next product rollout and cloud‑spending trends for direction.

stocks.name: NVIDIA
stocks.summary: NVIDIA fell 1.5% today, sitting 4.1% below its 52‑week high yet still 36.8% above its low, suggesting modest room to the upside. The stock is up 8.3% this month and 19.7% YTD, buoyed by AI demand. Key watch: the upcoming earnings report and GPU inventory levels.

stocks.name: Alphabet
stocks.summary: Alphabet slipped 3.8% on the day, now 16% under its 52‑week high but 43.2% above its low, indicating a sizable gap to the top. With a 2.9% monthly decline and 7.4% YTD gain, the stock is under pressure. Investors should monitor ad‑tech revenue trends and any regulatory developments.

stocks.name: Amazon
stocks.summary: Amazon dropped 2.2% today, trading 12.2% below its 52‑week high while still 25.4% above its low, leaving modest upside. The stock is down 4.9% this month but up 10.1% YTD, reflecting mixed momentum. Watch for Q4 sales guidance and cloud‑services performance as the next driver.

stocks.name: Meta Platforms
stocks.summary: Meta rose 1.0% on the day, just 1.8% shy of its 52‑week high and 41.8% above its low, positioning it near the top of its range. Strong 33.2% monthly gain and 14.7% YTD growth underscore robust momentum. Key focus: user growth metrics and monetization of AI features ahead of earnings.

stocks.name: Tesla
stocks.summary: Tesla edged up 0.3% today, still 22.4% below its 52‑week high but 27.4% above its low, indicating a wide upside cushion. The stock is up 8.9% this month yet down 13.2% YTD, reflecting recent weakness. Watch production updates and pricing strategy as the next inflection point.

stocks.name: Broadcom
stocks.summary: Broadcom fell 2.6% intraday, now 26% under its 52‑week high while 21.4% above its low, suggesting a sizable gap to the peak. Monthly performance is flat (-0.9%) with a modest 2.7% YTD gain. Investors should keep an eye on semiconductor demand cycles and the upcoming earnings release.

stocks.name: Advanced Micro Devices
stocks.summary: AMD slipped 1.5% today but remains just 1.5% below its 52‑week high, having surged 285.4% from its low and up 175% YTD, indicating a near‑peak rally. The stock posted a 34.6% monthly gain and a 19.9% weekly surge. Watch for GPU inventory trends and the next earnings beat as the primary catalyst.

stocks.name: Oracle
stocks.summary: Oracle has slipped 3.1% on the day and sits 53.4% below its 52‑week high, though it remains 25.7% above its 52‑week low, indicating a deep discount to recent peaks. The modest 1‑week gain masks broader weakness, and investors should watch upcoming earnings guidance for signs of a turnaround in cloud and AI services.

stocks.name: Salesforce
stocks.summary: Salesforce is marginally up 0.5% today, trading 10.1% below its 52‑week high but still 58.5% above its 52‑week low after a strong 13.8% monthly rally. The stock’s near‑term direction hinges on its ability to sustain growth in subscription revenue and any updates to its AI‑driven product roadmap.

stocks.name: JPMorgan Chase
stocks.summary: JPMorgan fell 0.7% and is 7.6% under its 52‑week high while still 20.5% above its 52‑week low, reflecting modest resilience in a volatile banking environment. Investors should focus on the bank’s loan‑growth trends and any impact from interest‑rate shifts on net interest margin.

stocks.name: Bank of America
stocks.summary: Bank of America slipped 0.4% and remains 13.2% below its 52‑week high, though 21.1% above its 52‑week low, indicating continued pressure on U.S. banks. Key watch points are credit‑quality metrics and the bank’s ability to capture higher rates without eroding loan demand.

stocks.name: Visa
stocks.summary: Visa dropped 2.3% and is 5.9% under its 52‑week high, still 22.8% above its 52‑week low, showing a modest pullback after a solid YTD gain. The next catalyst is payment‑volume growth and any shifts in consumer spending patterns that could affect transaction volumes.

stocks.name: Mastercard
stocks.summary: Mastercard is down 1.4% and sits 6.7% below its 52‑week high, 18.9% above its 52‑week low, with YTD performance essentially flat. Investors should monitor global transaction volume trends and the rollout of new fintech partnerships for upside potential.

stocks.name: Netflix
stocks.summary: Netflix fell 1.1% and is 42.5% below its 52‑week high, barely 5.6% above its 52‑week low, reflecting a steep decline from its peak. The critical watch item is subscriber growth in key international markets and the impact of price hikes on churn.

stocks.name: Eli Lilly
stocks.summary: Eli Lilly slipped 1.2% but remains 10.1% under its 52‑week high and a robust 62.1% above its 52‑week low, with a solid YTD gain. Investors should keep an eye on upcoming drug approvals and pricing dynamics for its blockbuster diabetes and obesity treatments.

stocks.name: UnitedHealth
stocks.summary: UnitedHealth dropped 1.7% and is 14.4% below its 52‑week high while still 45.1% above its 52‑week low, maintaining a healthy YTD rise. The key focus will be Medicare Advantage enrollment trends and any regulatory developments affecting its cost structure.

stocks.name: Johnson & Johnson
stocks.summary: Johnson & Johnson is trading just 3.3% below its 52‑week high and still 55.8% above its 52‑week low, with modest daily and weekly gains after a strong YTD rally of 31.9%. The stock’s near‑record level suggests investors are pricing in continued earnings momentum, but the next catalyst will be the upcoming earnings release and any guidance on its pharmaceutical pipeline.

stocks.name: Walmart
stocks.summary: Walmart sits 17.4% under its 52‑week high but remains 10.8% above its 52‑week low, posting modest daily and weekly gains while YTD performance is flat. The key watch point is whether its low‑price growth strategy can sustain momentum amid a slight YTD dip, especially after the next earnings report.

stocks.name: Costco
stocks.summary: Costco trades 17.2% below its 52‑week high yet 6.9% above its 52‑week low, with a small daily rise but a 4.5% monthly decline despite a 6.3% YTD gain. Investors should focus on membership renewal trends and any guidance on inventory pressures as the next earnings call approaches.

stocks.name: Home Depot
stocks.summary: Home Depot is 25.6% off its 52‑week high but barely above its 52‑week low, having slipped 2.9% over the week and 10.9% month‑to‑date, contributing to a 12.3% YTD decline. The next inflection point will be the upcoming earnings and any updates on housing market demand that could reverse the downtrend.

stocks.name: Exxon Mobil
stocks.summary: Exxon Mobil trades 4.8% below its 52‑week high while still 49.9% above its 52‑week low, posting a solid daily gain after a 2.3% monthly dip and a strong 34.1% YTD rise. The critical factor to watch is oil‑price dynamics and the company’s quarterly results, which will confirm if the rally can sustain.

stocks.name: Coca-Cola
stocks.summary: Coca‑Cola is 3.7% under its 52‑week high and 37.7% above its 52‑week low, with a modest daily rise despite a 2.7% monthly decline and a robust 29.9% YTD gain. Investors should monitor the upcoming earnings and any updates on pricing power and volume trends in the soft‑drink segment.

stocks.name: Walt Disney
stocks.summary: Disney trades 10% below its 52‑week high but remains 12.8% above its 52‑week low, with a 2.8% weekly drop and a 4% monthly decline, contributing to a 6.8% YTD loss.
